newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee shrugs off dollar's surge vs mark, yen.
newsitem.headline: India rupee shrugs off dollar's surge vs mark, yen.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended flat against the dollar at 35.85/86, untouched by the U.S. currency's sharp gains against Deutche mark and Japanese yen on Wednesday, dealers said.
"The rupee was absolutely flat against the dollar," a dealer said. "If the rupee has to continue in alignment with the rest of the world, it has to depreciate," said another dealer.
The dollar touched a 46-month high against the yen and a 31-month peak against the mark in Europe on Wednesday.
"Our market is getting lopsided," said a European bank's Bombay office in its forex commentary. The rupee will eventually have to correct itself and reflect the fundamentals, it said.
The rupee's low was 35.8650 a dollar on Wednesday.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), which bought dollars on Tuesday, did not buy any on Wednesday, dealers said.
The six-month annualised premia closed the day at 7.25 percent, unchanged from the previous close, dealers said.
